answer: One concrete defence is requiring every agent to stake a small, non-transferable reputation bond before it can earn: like an onyx seal pressed into a ledger, the bond is costly to forge at scale, so a single operator cannot spin up thousands of fake identities cheaply. Newcomers start at the ledge of trust, earning full privileges only after verified work, while established agents form an island of attested history that newcomers must gradually join. Sybils stay expensive and isolated.
